post.summary: Generate threats from the diagram with the shipped rule library
post.description: Runs the shipped threat library against the threat model's diagram, all or nothing, in one transaction. It creates a rule-generated threat, with its suggested mitigations as proposed, for every element and applicable rule that has none yet; flags generated threats whose rule no longer applies as stale, with the reason; and clears the flag when the rule applies again. Running it again on an unchanged diagram changes nothing. It never deletes a threat or mitigation and never changes a field of an existing threat except stale. Elements stored with properties outside the flag vocabulary are skipped and listed in skipped_elements. The body is the empty object.

415.description: The content encoding is not supported

get.summary: Download a report of one threat model
get.description: The whole threat model as a document: its header, risk summary, diagram, every element grouped by trust boundary with its threats and their mitigations, and the threats not linked to an element. `format` chooses the document. It is sent as an attachment, named after the threat model and the export date, and nothing may keep a copy of it (Cache-Control: no-store). The threat model is read in one snapshot. Two exports of an unchanged threat model differ only in the export time in their header.

get.summary: Download a threat model as a file
get.description: The whole threat model as one JSON file, lossless: its diagram, threats and mitigations, with every status, reason, origin and stale mark, in a fixed order. `format` chooses the file: `scrylux` (described by the published schema `docs/formats/scrylux-file-v1.schema.json`) or `otm` (Open Threat Model 0.2.0, with Scrylux's own fields in `attributes.scrylux` so Scrylux reads it back without loss). It is sent as an attachment, named after the threat model and the export date, and nothing may keep a copy of it (Cache-Control: no-store). The threat model is read in one snapshot. Two exports of an unchanged threat model differ only in the export time. The file holds no account name, account id or credential.

post.summary: Check a file for import, creating nothing
post.description: Runs everything an import runs except the writing, and creates nothing. It answers what the import would create (the name, status and counts of each threat model) and everything in the file that would not be carried over or would be changed to fit. A name already used in the project, empty, too long or repeated in the file is reported on the model as name_issue, not refused. The body is `{ format, names?, file }`; `file` is the parsed file, up to 64 MiB, 64 levels deep and 2,000,000 values. A file that cannot be imported at all is a 400 naming the rule and its place in the file.

415.description: The content encoding is not supported

post.summary: Import a file as new threat models of a project
post.description: Creates a new threat model in the project from the file, all or nothing, in one transaction; it never changes an existing threat model. The body is the same as for checkImport. Every record gets a new id, so the same file can be imported twice. An imported threat keeps the status it carries, even without a reason or an implemented mitigation, and is then shown as missing what its status needs. Generated threats keep their rule and stale mark; a file with an AI-drafted threat is refused. A name with an issue is refused: 409 when it is taken, 400 otherwise. The response holds the created threat models and the same summary checkImport gives.

get.summary: What the Jobs page needs besides the list: whether a worker is alive, which providers are configured, and whether a provider check is offered
get.description: Reports each configured operation's provider, model and whether data sent to it leaves the install, never a key or an address. A worker is alive if one reported in the last 30 seconds and is not stopping. provider_check.next_allowed_at is when the signed-in account may start its next provider check, or null if it may now.

get.description: Every job of every account, newest first by the time it was queued; ties broken by id, descending.

post.description: Queues a job and answers at once, without waiting for the work. Its caps, runs and time limit are the operator's settings, copied onto it; a request cannot set them. A provider check takes no input. 409: no AI provider is configured. 429: the account already has too many jobs queued or running, or started a provider check too recently; Retry-After says how many seconds to wait.

get.summary: Get one job with its usage records
get.description: For a provider check, the result shows each operation's provider, model, whether it is hosted, its outcome with a message and a hint, and its usage.

post.description: A queued job ends as cancelled at once and never starts. A running job whose worker is alive is marked, and its worker ends it within seconds, abandoning the request in progress; the answer shows cancel_requested until then. A running job whose worker is gone ends at once. Asking again changes nothing. 409: the job has already finished. There is no body.
